# Template variables, per service

These files record the environment variables each service carries **in the published
Railway template** — one `.env` per service. They are documentation and a working
reference for reproducing / auditing the template, not files consumed by any build.
The published template is the source of truth; keep these in sync when it changes.

## Layout

Services are grouped into subfolders mirroring the **service groups on the Railway
canvas**:

- `clickhouse/` — clickhouse, snuba-api, snuba-errors
- `data-plane/` — postgres, redis, kafka, memcached
- `sentry/` — gateway, sentry-web, sentry-workers, sentry-relay, sentry-taskbroker

## Variable descriptions (Railway raw-editor quirk)

Railway's template **Raw Editor** turns a `#` comment into a variable's description,
and it attaches each comment to the variable on the line **directly above** it — so
the description must sit on the line **below** its variable, with no blank line
between:

```
SENTRY_URL_PREFIX=https://${{ gateway.RAILWAY_PUBLIC_DOMAIN }}
# Public base URL; required for browser login/CSRF.
```

A comment placed *above* a variable is ignored (or captured by the previous one).
The header block at the top of each file is descriptive only and is not read.

## Conventions

- **Cross-service hostnames use references, never literals:**
  `${{ <service>.RAILWAY_PRIVATE_DOMAIN }}` (resolves to `<service>.railway.internal`).
  Ports/paths are appended as plain text, e.g. `${{ kafka.RAILWAY_PRIVATE_DOMAIN }}:9092`.
  This binds to the service and survives renames — no hardcoded hostname to go stale.
- **Shared secrets** are generated once on their owning service with `${{ secret(N) }}`
  and referenced elsewhere (e.g. `CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD` is generated on `clickhouse`,
  referenced as `${{ clickhouse.CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD }}` on the snuba services).
- **`RAILWAY_DOCKERFILE_PATH`** tells each build service which Dockerfile to use.

## Secrets policy

Never commit a real secret here. The relay keypair is the only value that can't be
generated by `secret()`; in these files it appears as a **placeholder**. The real
keypair lives only in the template definition on Railway (same rule as the gitignored
`relay/credentials.json`).
